Where is Cedar Rapids and how is the city divided?

Cedar Rapids is the county seat of Linn County, about 20 miles north of Iowa City and 128 miles northeast of Des Moines. It is the second most populous city in Iowa, with 137,710 residents in the 2020 census and a Census Bureau estimate of 137,935 for 2025.

The Cedar River splits the city into east and west sides, and 1st Avenue (U.S. Route 151 Business) splits it north from south. That makes four address quadrants. The city uses 14 ZIP codes, with downtown and Mays Island in 52401, so the first thing to confirm in any listing or offer is the exact quadrant and ZIP.

The city covers about 76 square miles at an elevation of 810 feet.

What is the history of Cedar Rapids?

Osgood Shepherd built the first cabin in 1837 or 1838, and the town was platted in 1841 as Rapids City. It was incorporated as Cedar Rapids on January 15, 1849, with fewer than 400 people.

Czech immigrants made up a large part of the early population: in 1856 about a quarter of roughly 1,600 residents were Czech. The first locomotive arrived on June 15, 1859. Sinclair meatpacking started in 1871 and the Quaker Oats mill was built in 1873. The county seat moved from Marion to Cedar Rapids in 1919.

Population passed 110,000 by 1970 and has grown slowly since, reaching 126,326 in 2010.

How did flooding and the 2020 derecho affect Cedar Rapids housing?

Cedar Rapids has two kinds of recent storm history that a seller needs to understand, river flooding and wind. Both left marks on the housing stock and on buyers' questions.

  • June 2008 flood: the Cedar River crested at a record 31.12 feet on June 13, against a previous record of 20 feet. Some 1,126 city blocks flooded, 7,749 properties were evacuated, including 5,900 homes, and at least 1,300 properties had to be demolished.
  • September 2016 flood: the river reached 22 feet on September 27, the second highest crest on record, with flood stage at 12 feet. More than 5,000 homes were affected. The city approved a $625 million, 20-year levee plan in 2015.
  • August 10, 2020 derecho: sustained winds of 60 to 80 mph and gusts of 110 mph or more hit the city. About 95 percent of Cedar Rapids lost power and 20 schools were damaged.

If a house sits in an area that took water or wind damage, expect a conventional buyer's inspection to look hard at the basement, roof and electrical system. A cash purchase can skip that repair negotiation.

Who are the largest employers in Cedar Rapids?

Collins Aerospace is the largest employer in Cedar Rapids, with between 5,000 and 9,999 employees according to the city's 2024 annual financial report as summarized on Wikipedia. Aegon USA keeps its U.S. headquarters in the city.

Grain processing is the largest sector, with about 4,000 direct jobs averaging $85,000 a year and about 8,000 indirect jobs. In February 2025, Quality Technology Services announced a $750 million data center expected to create about 30 jobs.

Which Cedar Rapids neighborhoods and school districts matter to sellers?

Cedar Rapids has twelve active neighborhood associations, and the ones nearest downtown include Wellington Heights, Oakhill Jackson and Moundview. Other named areas are Noelridge Park and Kenwood Park, plus informal districts such as Czech Village, New Bohemia (NewBo), Kingston Village and Wilderness Estates.

Four school districts serve parts of the city, and the address decides which one applies:

  • Cedar Rapids Community School District, with 15,589 students in 2023-24, 21 elementary schools, 6 middle schools and 5 high schools.
  • Linn-Mar Community School District, serving part of the northeast quadrant.
  • College Community School District, serving part of the southwest quadrant.
  • Marion Independent School District, serving a portion of the city.

What roads, rail and weather affect a Cedar Rapids house?

Interstate 380 runs north and south through the city as part of the Avenue of the Saints. U.S. 30, 151 and 218 and Iowa 13 and 100 also serve it, and the Eastern Iowa Airport is the regional airport. Four railroads run through town: Union Pacific, Crandic, Canadian National and Iowa Northern.

The climate is humid continental. Average precipitation is 35.91 inches a year and average snowfall is 26.7 inches, based on 1991 to 2020 normals at the airport. The record low is minus 30 degrees on January 31, 2019, and the record high is 110 degrees on July 6, 1911. Roofs, gutters and heating systems take real wear in that range.

What rental registration rules does Cedar Rapids have?

Cedar Rapids requires rental housing to hold a Certificate of Compliance before it can be legally occupied. The city issues it once the property meets the Housing Code and registration and inspection charges are paid.

Annual registration fees on the city's rental housing page are $50 for a single-family unit or condominium, $60 for a duplex, and $42 plus $13 per unit for a multi-family structure. A separate inspection fee schedule took effect July 1, 2023.

A landlord who is tired of managing a rental house can sell it with tenants in place or after they move out. Ask the buyer whether the registration will transfer or needs to be filed again.

What does Iowa require at a Cedar Rapids closing?

Every Iowa deed that moves through the Linn County Recorder carries a declaration of value, and most also carry a groundwater hazard statement. Iowa Code 558.69 sets out what the seller must report.

  • Wells, with approximate location and whether they meet state rules.
  • Private burial sites, underground storage tanks and known hazardous waste.
  • Solid waste disposal sites identified by the Department of Natural Resources.
  • Private sewage disposal systems, and whether they were inspected or are exempt at transfer.

At least one seller or the seller's agent signs it, and the buyer receives a copy. The owner is responsible for the accuracy of the answers. After the 2008 flood, owners of older properties should check records carefully for any tank or well that was removed, capped or replaced.

How does a cash sale of a Cedar Rapids house work?

You can sell a Cedar Rapids house for cash without repairs, showings or a lender's appraisal. The steps are short.

  1. Send the address and a few details about the condition and any tenants.
  2. Receive a written offer based on the house as it stands.
  3. If the offer works, pick a closing date and let a title company prepare the deed, declaration of value and groundwater statement.
  4. Close, and record at the county.

Property taxes in Iowa turn delinquent on October 1 and April 1 for the two installments under Iowa Code 445.37, so ask the Linn County Treasurer what is paid before the closing date.

More questions about Cedar Rapids, IA

How many people live in Cedar Rapids?

The 2020 census counted 137,710 residents in Cedar Rapids, and the Census Bureau estimate for July 1, 2025 is 137,935. It is the second most populous city in Iowa.

How high did the Cedar River get in the 2008 flood?

The Cedar River crested at a record 31.12 feet on June 13, 2008. The earlier record was 20 feet, and 7,749 properties, including 5,900 homes, were evacuated.

Do landlords need a permit in Cedar Rapids?

Yes. Rental housing needs a Certificate of Compliance to be legally occupied, and registration fees are $50 a year for a single-family unit or condo, $60 for a duplex, and $42 plus $13 per unit for multi-family buildings.

Which school district is my Cedar Rapids house in?

It depends on the address. Cedar Rapids Community Schools serves most of the city, while Linn-Mar, College Community and Marion Independent serve parts of it.

Who is the biggest employer in Cedar Rapids?

Collins Aerospace, with between 5,000 and 9,999 employees in the city's 2024 report, followed by Aegon USA, the school district and the city itself in the 1,000 to 4,999 range.

Where is Davenport, Iowa, and what is the Quad Cities?

Davenport is the county seat of Scott County and sits on the Mississippi River at the eastern edge of Iowa. It is one of the five Quad Cities, together with Bettendorf in Iowa and Rock Island, Moline and East Moline in Illinois.

The city covers about 66 square miles at an elevation of 660 feet. The river runs east to west here, and the ground slopes up to the north. The 2020 census counted 101,724 residents, which makes Davenport the third most populous city in Iowa after Des Moines and Cedar Rapids. The metro area had 381,801 people.

What is the history of Davenport?

Antoine Le Claire settled Davenport on May 14, 1836, and named it for George Davenport. The city was incorporated on January 25, 1839. The 1832 Black Hawk Purchase, covering about 6 million acres for $640,000, had opened the land to settlement.

The first railroad bridge across the Mississippi opened in 1856 and linked Davenport to Rock Island, Illinois. Abraham Lincoln was the railroad's lead defense lawyer in the litigation that followed a steamboat collision that May. Past industries here included locomotive manufacturing, meatpacking and a Caterpillar loader plant that later closed.

The population has hovered around 100,000 for about four decades, and the 2024 estimate of 100,938 sits right on that line. A flat population means sellers here are not counting on a surge of newcomers, so condition and price carry the sale.

How serious is flooding in Davenport?

Davenport has no permanent flood wall or levee, which makes it the largest city on the Mississippi River without one. The older flood wall dates from 1919.

  • The city requires new construction in the floodplain to be elevated or protected by walls.
  • The 1993 Great Flood crested at 22.63 feet on July 9, nearly 8 feet above flood stage.
  • The river flooded again in 2019 and 2023, while higher walls protected downtown Rock Island and Bettendorf in 2019.
  • Credit Island stayed closed for 5.5 months after the 2008 flooding.

Anyone selling a riverside house should expect buyers to ask whether the lot is in a floodplain and whether the house has ever taken water. A cash buyer will ask the same questions but can price the answer in directly.

Which employers drive the Davenport economy?

Manufacturing is the largest employment sector in Davenport, with more than 7,600 jobs. John Deere is the largest single employer in the Quad Cities, with 7,200 workers in the area and 948 at its north Davenport plant.

EmployerWorkers
Genesis Health System5,125 total, 4,900 in Davenport
Trinity Regional Health System3,333
Hy-Vee3,138
Davenport Community School District2,237

Von Maur and Lee Enterprises are both headquartered in Davenport. The Rock Island Arsenal, KONE and Alcoa are major employers elsewhere in the metro area.

Which Davenport neighborhoods have a distinct character?

Davenport has several historic districts, and a house inside one may come with expectations about its look and age. Three stand out in the record.

  • Hamburg Historic District: home to the most architecturally significant residences in the old German neighborhoods.
  • Vander Veer Park Historic District: anchored by Vander Veer Park, modeled on New York's Central Park.
  • Village of East Davenport: its Lindsay Park was a Civil War parade ground for Camp McClellan.

The east side has long held higher-end housing. Whatever the area, a seller of an older Davenport house should gather permits, repair receipts and any flood history before talking to buyers.

What school district and colleges serve Davenport?

The Davenport Community School District serves nearly 14,500 students across Davenport, Blue Grass, Buffalo and Walcott and is the fourth largest district in Iowa. It runs four public high schools (Central, West, Mid City and North), six intermediate schools and 23 elementary schools. Assumption is the private high school.

Higher education includes St. Ambrose University, founded in 1882, Palmer College of Chiropractic, Kaplan University and Hamilton Technical College. A house near any of these campuses or schools may draw a different set of buyers than one near the river, so describe the location plainly when you talk to a buyer.

How do roads, bridges and weather affect a Davenport house?

Three bridges link Davenport to Illinois: the Government Bridge, the Centennial Bridge and the I-280 Bridge. Interstates 80, 74 and 280 serve the city, along with U.S. 6, 61 and 67 and Iowa 22 and 130. The closest commercial airport is Quad City International in Moline.

The climate is humid continental, with warm humid summers and cold windy winters. Average precipitation is 36.17 inches a year. The record high is 111 degrees on July 12, 1936 and the record low is minus 29 degrees on January 18, 2009. That spread is hard on roofs, siding and older furnaces.

What taxes and filings apply when a Davenport house sells?

The main Iowa cost at recording is the real estate transfer tax. Iowa Code 428A.1 sets it at 80 cents per $500 of value. For a house valued at $200,000, that is $320 (400 units of $500 at 80 cents). The tax does not apply when no consideration is paid.

Property tax is separate. Under Iowa Code 445.37, the first installment is delinquent from October 1 and the second from April 1. Payments sent online must be entered by midnight on the last day of the month before the delinquent date, with a weekend rule that moves the deadline.

  • Ask the Scott County Treasurer which installments are paid.
  • Have the title company prorate the current bill to the closing date.
  • Confirm the groundwater hazard statement is signed.

What should a Davenport seller gather before talking to buyers?

A short folder of records answers most buyer questions about a Davenport house. The list below follows from the flood and age facts above.

  • Any flood insurance policy, claim or repair receipt, since the Mississippi flooded in 1993, 2008, 2019 and 2023.
  • Elevation or floodplain information for the lot, because new floodplain construction must be raised or walled.
  • Records on wells, tanks or a septic system for the groundwater hazard statement.
  • Lease copies and rent status if tenants live in the house.

If a house needs more repair than you want to fund, say so up front. A cash buyer prices the work, while a conventional buyer's inspection usually turns it into a negotiation.

How does a cash sale of a Davenport house work?

A cash sale in Davenport skips the listing, the open houses and the lender's timeline. You share the address and the condition of the house, review a written offer, and pick a closing date that suits you.

A title company or attorney then prepares the deed and filings, the buyer pays at closing, and the deed is recorded in Scott County. You can say no to the offer at no cost, and you should compare it with what you would net from a listing after repairs and agent costs.

More questions about Davenport, IA

How many people live in Davenport, Iowa?

The 2020 census counted 101,724 people in Davenport, and the Census Bureau estimates 100,358 as of July 1, 2025. It is the third most populous city in Iowa.

Does Davenport have a flood wall?

No permanent flood wall or levee protects the city, which makes it the largest city on the Mississippi without one. New construction in the floodplain must be elevated or walled.

What is the transfer tax on a Davenport home sale?

Iowa charges 80 cents per $500 of value under Iowa Code 428A.1, so a $200,000 value produces $320. No tax applies when there is no consideration.

Who are the largest employers in Davenport?

John Deere is the largest employer in the Quad Cities, with 948 workers at its north Davenport plant. Genesis Health System has 4,900 employees in Davenport, and the school district has 2,237.

When are Iowa property taxes delinquent?

The first installment is delinquent from October 1 and the second from April 1, with a weekend rule that moves the date to the second business day of the month.

Where is Ankeny, Iowa, and how is it laid out?

Ankeny is in north-central Polk County and is a suburb of Des Moines. Interstate 35 runs along the east side, and U.S. Route 69 runs through the center of town.

The city covers about 32.8 square miles at an elevation near 988 feet. As of 2018 it maintained 543 miles of road and 72 traffic signals, which gives a sense of how much of the city is newer, spread-out development.

When you describe a house to a buyer, give the nearest main road. Distance to I-35 or U.S. 69 is one of the first facts a buyer from the Des Moines area will ask about.

How did Ankeny grow from a small town into Iowa's fifth-largest city?

John Fletcher Ankeny and Sarah Ankeny founded the town on April 22, 1875, on 80 acres they bought on July 11, 1874, for $1,600. Ankeny was incorporated as a town on February 28, 1903, and became a city in 1961.

In 1941 an ordnance plant took land here. It operated from 1942 to 1945, and Deere and Company bought the factory in 1947. Deere is still on the employer list today.

Ankeny is now the fifth-most populous city in Iowa. The population more than doubled between 2000 and 2020, so many houses here were built in that stretch, and their roofs, furnaces and water heaters are now reaching an age where replacement decisions come up.

What are the largest employers in Ankeny?

Ankeny Community Schools is the largest employer by headcount, at 1,965 people, followed by Deere and Company with 1,900.

  • Perishable Distributors of Iowa: 687
  • Des Moines Area Community College: 611

In 2019 the largest industry sectors were education and health care at 23.3%, finance, insurance and real estate at 14.1%, and retail at 12.0%. The median household income was $102,518 in the 2024 American Community Survey, according to Wikipedia's summary. A seller whose job is changing, or who is relocating for work with one of these employers, may need to close on a specific date, and a cash sale can be scheduled around that date.

Which school districts serve Ankeny?

Most of the city is in the Ankeny Community School District, the sixth-largest district in Iowa with nearly 12,000 students and 16 buildings.

Parts of the city are served by the Saydel and North Polk community school districts. If you are describing a house to a buyer, confirm the district for the specific address on the district's own boundary tools, because the line does not follow city limits.

Des Moines Area Community College opened its Ankeny campus in 1967 on 240 acres. The campus now covers 304 acres, and DMACC serves over 15,000 students across its locations.

What is Prairie Trail, and why do Ankeny sellers hear about it?

Prairie Trail is a large planned development built on a former Iowa State University research plot. The city bought the land in June 2005 for $23.6 million and sold it to developer Dennis Albaugh in September 2005.

As part of that deal, the city agreed to invest up to $20 million in basic infrastructure. The result is a district with its own streets, utilities and commercial space. Homes in newer developments like this one often have different covenants, association dues or special assessments than older houses near the center of town. Ask the title company to pull those records before you set a closing date.

How does Ankeny weather affect houses here?

Ankeny has a hot-summer humid continental climate. Average annual precipitation is about 37 inches and average annual snowfall is about 25 inches.

The record high is 106 degrees Fahrenheit and the record low is minus 34. A house here has to handle both extremes, so the furnace, the air conditioner, the roof and the sump pump all do real work. If any of those are near the end of their life, a cash sale lets you sell without replacing them.

What should you gather before contacting a buyer in Ankeny?

A short list of documents makes an Ankeny sale faster because the title company can start work the day you accept an offer.

  • The names exactly as they appear on the current deed, and a copy of the deed if you have one.
  • The latest property tax statement, so the closing agent can check for unpaid installments.
  • The mortgage lender name and an approximate payoff, if there is a loan.
  • Any homeowner association contact, since newer subdivisions often have one.
  • A list of known problems with the roof, plumbing, electrical or foundation.

Polk County is the county that records the deed and administers the tax records for the city, so your parcel will be found under Polk County rather than a separate Ankeny office.

What if the Ankeny house is inherited or has several owners?

Every owner of record has to agree to the sale and sign the deed. If an owner has died, the estate has to be opened or the title has to be cleared another way before the house can transfer.

That step is usually the longest part of an inherited sale, and it does not depend on whether the buyer pays cash. What a cash buyer changes is everything after it: there is no lender review, no appraisal to schedule and no repair negotiation. If the heirs live in different places, they can sign separately and the closing can happen without everyone traveling to Ankeny.

Tell us who the heirs are, whether a will exists and whether the estate has been opened. We will tell you what the title company is likely to ask for.

How does a cash sale work for an Ankeny house?

A cash sale in Ankeny is a direct purchase with no lender, so it can close on a date you choose once title work is complete.

  • You send the address and describe the condition, including any repairs you have skipped.
  • We review the property and give you a written offer you can accept or decline.
  • A title company prepares the deed, the declaration of value and the groundwater hazard statement or its exemption sentence. The Scott County Recorder's page spells out these Iowa deed requirements, and they come from state law.
  • Transfer tax applies to the sale price over $500 unless the deed states an exemption.
  • The deed is recorded with the Polk County Recorder, because Ankeny is in Polk County.

If the house is part of an estate or has more than one owner, every owner has to sign. Tell us early if there are co-owners, because that is the most common reason a closing date slips.

Where is Ames, Iowa, and how did the city start?

It was named for Oakes Ames, a Massachusetts congressman who helped build the transcontinental railroad, and was founded by Cynthia Olive Duff and the railroad figure John Insley Blair. Ames was incorporated on December 20, 1869, and William West became the first mayor in 1870.

The 2020 census counted 66,427 residents, which made Ames the ninth-most populous city in Iowa. For a seller, the railroad-era street grid near downtown and the newer growth farther out mean very different houses under the same city name.

Iowa State University shapes it more than any other single institution. The university was founded in 1856, and fall 2023 enrollment was 30,177 students, roughly half the size of the city's resident population.

Campustown, just south of the campus, is a high-density mixed-use area with student apartments, restaurants and nightlife. Ames Main Street and Old Town are the city's historic districts. Because so much of that housing is rented, the city's rental rules come up in many Ames sales.

Owner-occupied means a townhouse, condo or detached home lived in by the owner or a first-degree relative. One roomer, one exchange student, or a live-in nanny or nurse is allowed. More than one of those makes the unit a rental. If a tenant is buying the home on contract, owner-occupied status requires a legally recorded contract with the Story County Recorder.

If you stopped renting the house, ask the Inspection Division to confirm the removal form went through. Otherwise fees keep accruing in your name.

The owner, a registered operator or an authorized representative has to be present, and a tenant does not count as a representative. The owner or operator must give tenants at least 24 hours' notice. Some property types are exempt from registration: owner-occupied single-family homes, licensed bed and breakfasts, hotels and motels, university housing, state-licensed health and custodial facilities, and fraternity and sorority houses. The deed also needs a groundwater hazard statement, or a sentence on the first page saying the transaction is exempt from that requirement. Since July 1, 2022, a seller can use the exemption if none of the listed conditions exist on the property. A recorder cannot record a deed without one or the other.

Where is Council Bluffs, Iowa, and what is the Loess Hills setting?

Council Bluffs is the seat of Pottawattamie County, on the east bank of the Missouri River directly across from Omaha, Nebraska. A small part of the city reaches into Mills County.

The city lies in the Loess Hills, so the ground rolls and drops in a way most of Iowa does not. It covers about 46 square miles at 978 feet, and Lake Manawa State Park sits at the southern edge. Viewpoints include Fairmont Park, Kirn Park, the Lincoln Monument and the Lewis and Clark Monument. The 2020 census counted 62,799 people, and the 2024 estimate is 62,665.

How did Council Bluffs get its name and start?

Lewis and Clark named the bluff after a meeting with the Otoe on August 2, 1804. The town itself was called Kanesville until about 1852 or 1853, and it was incorporated as Council Bluffs on January 19, 1853.

  • 1840s: Fort Croghan was built in 1842 and destroyed by a flood the same year. Latter-day Saints arrived in large numbers from 1846, and Kanesville became the main outfitting point and head of the Mormon Trail.
  • 1860s: Lincoln designated Council Bluffs the starting point of the transcontinental railroad, completed in 1869. The Chicago and North Western arrived in 1867.
  • 1870s and later: the Union Pacific Missouri River Bridge opened in 1872. By the 1930s the city was the fifth largest rail center in the country.

Mile 0 of the line is marked by a gold spike monument at 21st Street and 9th Avenue.

Data centers, casinos, rail and food processing all matter here. Google finished the first phase of its Council Bluffs data centers in 2009, and a third phase announced in March 2014 brought its investment to $1.5 billion. Google reported more than 300 jobs on site as of June 2016.

The casino sector began with Bluffs Run Greyhound Park in 1986 and riverboat casinos in the mid-1990s. Ameristar, Harrah's and Horseshoe operate here, and gambling revenue reached nearly $434 million by 2005, making it the 19th largest casino market in the country.

Interstate 80 and Interstate 29 meet at Council Bluffs, and U.S. 6 and 275 and Iowa 92 and 192 also serve the city. The Loess Hills National Scenic Byway passes through. The Interstate 480 bridge connects to downtown Omaha.

Anyone selling near the river should keep that in mind, since the river has moved the boundaries here before.

Property tax in Iowa is billed in two installments that turn delinquent on October 1 and April 1. Iowa Code 445.37 adds timing rules that apply to Council Bluffs owners.

  • If September 30 or March 31 falls on a weekend, delinquency moves to the second business day of the next month.
  • To avoid interest on mailed payments, the treasurer must receive the check by the last business day of the month before the delinquent date, or it must be postmarked before that date.
  • Online payments through a county treasurer's authorized site follow their own cutoff at midnight.

If you sell mid-year, the title company usually prorates the bill. Confirm what has been paid with the Pottawattamie County Treasurer first.

If none of the listed conditions exist, no separate statement is filed. The first page of the deed carries a prescribed line saying so instead. A recorder must refuse a deed that is missing the required statement. The transfer tax under Iowa Code 428A.1 is 80 cents per $500 and does not apply when no consideration is paid.

  • Notes on any well, buried tank or septic system, for the groundwater hazard statement.
  • The deed and any prior survey, so the title company can finish its search.

Iowa adds a few filings to a sale that Cedar Falls owners should plan for. Each one is set by statute and handled through the county recorder.

  • Real estate transfer tax: under Iowa Code 428A.1 the tax is 80 cents for each $500 of value, or fraction of $500, and it does not apply when there is no consideration. The statute does not say which side pays, so the purchase agreement decides.
  • Declaration of value: this form goes to the recorder with the deed. Iowa Code 428A.2 lists the transfers that are excused from it.
  • Groundwater hazard statement: under Iowa Code 558.69, the seller reports wells, burial sites, underground tanks, hazardous waste, solid waste disposal sites and private sewage systems on the property.

The recorder must refuse a deed that is missing a required statement. Recorders cannot charge a fee for filing the groundwater statement.

When do Black Hawk County property taxes become delinquent?

Iowa property tax is paid in two installments, and each one turns delinquent on a fixed day. The first installment is delinquent from October 1 and the second from April 1, according to Iowa Code 445.37.

If September 30 or March 31 lands on a weekend, delinquency moves to the second business day of the next month. A payment mailed with correct postage must be postmarked before the delinquent date to avoid interest.

When a Cedar Falls house sells in the middle of a tax year, the buyer and seller normally split the bill by the closing date. The county treasurer can confirm what has been paid so the closing figures match.

What problems do Cedar Falls sellers usually run into?

Most delays come from paperwork about the property itself, plus whatever work an older house needs. The city has been growing since the 1840s, and the population jumped sharply between 1950 and 1980, so houses of very different ages and conditions sit side by side.

  • A private well, septic system or buried tank that has to be disclosed on the groundwater hazard statement.
  • A house with deferred repairs that makes a traditional buyer's inspection list long.
  • A tenant in place or a lease that ends at a bad time.
  • An inherited home where the title is not yet in the heirs' names.

Each of these can slow a conventional sale. Selling to a cash buyer removes the loan appraisal step, though the recorder filings above still apply.

How does a cash sale of a Cedar Falls house work?

A cash sale in Cedar Falls follows the same recording steps as any other sale, with fewer moving parts before closing. You describe the house, the buyer reviews it, and an offer is made on the house as it stands.

  1. Share the address and condition of the house.
  2. Review the written offer and ask any question about it.
  3. If you accept, a title company or attorney prepares the deed, the declaration of value and the groundwater hazard statement.
  4. Sign, record at the Black Hawk County Recorder, and receive the proceeds.

You can decline an offer and owe nothing. Compare it with the cost and time of listing before you decide.

More questions about Cedar Falls, IA

How many people live in Cedar Falls, Iowa?

The Census Bureau estimates 41,240 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 40,713, which ranked Cedar Falls 13th among Iowa cities.

Is Cedar Falls in Black Hawk County?

Yes. Cedar Falls is in Black Hawk County and is part of the Waterloo-Cedar Falls metropolitan area. It was the first county seat in 1853, before an April 1855 referendum moved the seat to Waterloo.

What transfer tax applies when I sell a house in Cedar Falls?

Iowa charges 80 cents for each $500 of value, or fraction of $500, under Iowa Code 428A.1. No tax applies when there is no consideration. For a hypothetical $200,000 value, that works out to $320, and the contract sets who pays it.

Do I have to disclose a well or septic system when selling in Cedar Falls?

Yes, if the property has one. Iowa Code 558.69 requires a groundwater hazard statement that reports wells, private sewage systems, underground tanks, burial sites and certain waste conditions. If none exist, the deed carries a short statement saying so.

When is the second property tax installment delinquent in Iowa?

It becomes delinquent on April 1. If March 31 falls on a weekend, delinquency starts on the second business day of April.

Where is Bettendorf, Iowa?

Bettendorf is a city in Scott County on the Mississippi River, next to Davenport and across the river from Moline, East Moline and Rock Island, Illinois. It is one of the five Quad Cities.

The city covers about 22.4 square miles, of which 21.3 are land and 1.1 are water, at an elevation of roughly 666 feet. The 2020 census counted 39,102 residents, which ranked Bettendorf 15th in Iowa. A 2022 estimate put the figure at 39,548, up from 33,217 in 2010. The median age in 2020 was 39.9.

The city council has five wards and two at-large seats. Property in the city is assessed through the Scott County Assessor, since only Davenport runs its own assessor.

How did Bettendorf get its name and its start?

The land came to the United States after the Black Hawk War, through the 1832 Black Hawk Purchase from the Sac and Fox. It was then part of Wisconsin Territory.

Settlers founded two villages, Lilienthal and Gilbert, which merged into the town of Gilbert. Most residents were German immigrants. Around 1900 the town gave William and Joseph Bettendorf 70 acres of riverfront land so they could move their iron wagon business from Davenport. In 1903 the town of 440 people incorporated and took the brothers' name.

The city's later growth came from the riverfront industries described below, and the population rose from 33,217 in 2010 to 39,102 in 2020.

What drives the Bettendorf economy?

Manufacturing, the river and the casino industry have each had a turn. In the late 1940s the Aluminum Company of America chose Riverdale, an enclave of Bettendorf, for what was then described as the world's largest aluminum mill. It created thousands of jobs and fueled population growth.

Riverboat casinos debuted in Bettendorf on April 1, 1991, founded by Bernard Goldstein, who later founded Isle of Capri Casinos. The Quad Cities Waterfront Convention Center opened in 2009. The city owns it and Isle of Capri operates it. Alter Companies, run by the Goldstein family, operates scrap metal, barge and towboat businesses on the waterfront.

Wikipedia does not list current major employers for Bettendorf, so this page does not either. Scott Community College in Riverdale and an Upper Iowa University Quad Cities Center are the higher-education sites in the city.

Which school districts serve Bettendorf?

Two districts serve the city, and the address decides which one. That is worth checking before you describe a house to a buyer.

DistrictArea covered
Bettendorf Community School DistrictMost of central, northern and western Bettendorf; operates Bettendorf High School
Pleasant Valley Community School DistrictEastern Bettendorf, plus Pleasant Valley, Riverdale and LeClaire

Edison Academy is a consortium alternative high school in downtown Bettendorf. Private schools include Rivermont Collegiate, Lourdes Catholic School and Morning Star Academy.

How do the I-74 bridge and river flooding affect Bettendorf sellers?

The I-74 Bridge ties Bettendorf to Moline, Illinois. The original twin spans opened in 1935 and 1959, and a $1.2 billion replacement project that began in July 2017 was completed in 2021. It turned Grant Street near I-74 into a two-way street with three lanes in each direction.

Flooding is the other local fact a seller should know. Wikipedia reports that the city lies along the river and experiences frequent flooding and annual stormwater runoff. A 2000 study of 14 drainageways found 169 inlets inadequate for heavy rainfall, with Crow, Pigeon and Spencer creeks named as problem areas.

  • If the house is near one of those creeks, expect questions about basement water.
  • Keep any repair receipts for sump pumps, drain tile or waterproofing.
  • Ask your insurer for the flood zone designation before you list the property.

A cash buyer purchases the house in its present condition, wet basement included, which spares you from repairing something a lender-financed buyer would ask you to fix first.

What is the Bettendorf rental license rule?

Landlords in Bettendorf must hold a current rental registration and pass a rental inspection before renting residential property. The registration goes on file with the City Clerk before an inspection can be scheduled, and the city offers an online form.

An inspection certificate is issued once the structure is found to comply with the city code. To schedule, email CodeEnforcement@bettendorf.org or call the code enforcement hotline at (563) 344-4064 and leave a message. City Hall is at 1609 State Street, Bettendorf, IA 52722, and the main number is (563) 344-4000.

The program page does not state the inspection cycle, the fees or what happens when a rental property is sold, so ask the city or read the rental housing code before closing. If you are selling a rented house, tell us at the start so we can find out what the city needs.

How do Scott County tax payments work for a Bettendorf owner?

Bettendorf owners pay property tax to the Scott County Treasurer, which collects in two equal installments due September 30 and March 31. Taxes are certified in July or August.

The Treasurer has two offices in Davenport: the Administrative Center at 600 W. 4th St. and the General Store at 902 W. Kimberly Rd., Suite 6D. You can pay online by e-check for $0.25 or by credit card at 2.25%. Cash and checks carry no fee at the counter, and debit cards at the counter cost $2.00 per transaction. Interest starts the first business day after a due date.

If taxes stay unpaid, they are published in June and sold at the tax sale on the third Monday of June. A seller with an open installment can clear it at closing, but do not wait until the publication date to ask for a payoff figure.

What should a Bettendorf seller prepare before asking for an offer?

Have a few basic facts ready so the first conversation can end with a clear next step.

  • Which school district the address falls in, since two districts split the city.
  • Whether the house is near Crow, Pigeon or Spencer creek, or has ever had water in the basement.
  • Whether the house is rented, and if so, whether it has a rental registration and an inspection certificate.
  • Which tax installments you have paid, and whether any are open.
  • The names on the deed and any mortgage payoff.

With those answers, the title company can tell us quickly whether the closing can be set for a date that suits you.

What does a Bettendorf cash sale look like?

A cash sale in Bettendorf skips the lender, so closing depends mostly on title work and your schedule.

  • You send the address and the condition of the house.
  • We review it and send a written offer, which you can accept or decline.
  • A title company prepares the deed, the declaration of value, and the groundwater hazard statement or its exemption sentence.
  • Because Bettendorf is in Scott County, the deed goes to the Scott County Recorder, whose recording page lists the transfer tax rule on the sale price over $500.

Property tax in Scott County is due in two installments, September 30 and March 31. Any open installment is settled at closing out of the sale proceeds.

More questions about Bettendorf, IA

How many people live in Bettendorf?

The 2020 census counted 39,102 residents, and a 2022 estimate was 39,548. That ranked Bettendorf 15th among Iowa cities in 2020.

Which county is Bettendorf in?

Scott County. The deed is recorded with the Scott County Recorder.

Which school districts serve Bettendorf?

The Bettendorf Community School District covers most of central, northern and western Bettendorf, and the Pleasant Valley Community School District covers the eastern part.

Does Bettendorf require rental registration?

Yes. Landlords need a current rental registration on file with the City Clerk and must pass an inspection before renting. Contact code enforcement at (563) 344-4064.

Is flooding a concern in Bettendorf?

It can be. Wikipedia reports frequent flooding along the river and annual stormwater runoff, with Crow, Pigeon and Spencer creeks named as problem areas in a 2000 drainage study.

Can I sell a Bettendorf house with a wet basement or other damage?

Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so you do not need to repair water damage first. Disclose known issues accurately.
